quotes.quote: Sentiment-Analysis-7B is a 7B-parameter autoregressive language model fine-tuned for sentiment classification of user messages directed at a service, product, or agent (the "Target").
It is built on top of mistralai/Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2 and was fine-tuned with reinforcement learning, using an LLM as a judge, on a small internal training set of ~300 examples.
No pre-defined labels were used for training.
Given a user message, the model generates a response in the following format: the first token is the sentiment label (Negative, Neutral, or Positive), followed by a short explanation of the decision.
The evaluation metric used is accuracy. The following compares the base model with the fine-tuned model.
mistralai/Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2 62.0%
Sentiment-Analysis-7B (ours) 72.8%
The model is a causal language model and is loaded with AutoModelForCausalLM.
The sentiment label is always the first generated token, so setting max_new_tokens=3 returns the label only.
Use the system prompt below, which defines the "Target" and the sentiment rules.
Return sentiment of user message as Positive/Neutral/Negative and explanation.
Definition of "Target": the current service, product, or agent the user is interacting with (including its website, app, API, or support).
Negative, the user states an inability to log in, which is a failure related to the Target.

Microsoft uploaded Sentiment-Analysis-7B weights on October 20.
Based on a seven-billion-parameter Mistral model, it uses reinforcement learning with roughly 300 internal examples and rewards from an LLM judge.
Microsoft reports accuracy rising from 62.0% to 72.8%.
Roughly 300 refers to internal training examples, not evaluation-set size.
Microsoft does not disclose the latter; 72.8% is not an expected accuracy across languages or businesses.
The task concerns a user's attitude toward the current service, product, or agent—not generic sentence sentiment.
